description:
Problem. Since the cut-over (#2758, 2026-10-09 00:16 UTC) the oracle is the required soundness reviewer, but every review it posts opens with `### oracle-review-shadow: <state> for <sha>`, its commit status context is `oracle-review-shadow`, and its workflow, run names, artifacts and log lines all say shadow. Readers take "shadow" to mean the result is advisory. The name was kept on purpose through the cut-over because the required checker and the soundness merge digest parse the first line byte for byte.

Decision (owner, 2026-10-09). Rename it.

Where the name lives on develop e7eb5ce7e (re-check with `git grep -n oracle-review-shadow` before starting):
- Posted text: the first line in _project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/report.py; `status_context` in .github/oracle-reviewers.yml; job-summary and error prefixes and the argparse `prog` in cli.py.
- Parsers: `_ORACLE_VERDICT` and `ORACLE_CONTEXT` in _project/scripts/oracle_review_check.py; the first-line parser in _project/scripts/soundness_merge_digest.py.
- Identifiers with state behind them: `STATE_ARTIFACT_PREFIX` ("oracle-review-shadow-state-") and `WORKFLOW_PATH` in github.py, `WORKFLOW_FILE` in cli.py, the workflow file .github/workflows/oracle-review-shadow.yml, its `name:`, `run-name:`, concurrency group and plan/attempt artifact names; the gate-path entry for the workflow in .github/oracle-reviewers.yml.
- Docs and commands: oracle-review-v2.md, soundness-drain.md, merge-queue-governance.md, dev-loop-property-ledger.md, the 2026-10-05 decision record (amend, do not rewrite), Makefile references, tests and tests/fixtures/oracle_reviewers/pr2769_history.json.

Required behaviour.
1. New reviews open with `### <new-name>: <state> for <sha>` and post the new status context.
2. The required checker accepts both the old and the new first line. Old-format acceptance stays until no open pull request's latest oracle review uses the old line; record that condition and file a follow-up item (with `not_before` at least 14 days after merge) to remove it.
3. The merge digest accepts both first lines permanently, because it reads merged history.
4. Retry state survives the rename: the plan step reads the newest state artifact under the new name or, when none exists, under the old prefix and old workflow path, so the strike floor, retry budget and backoff carry over. The round history needs no change (it is read from the hidden protocol markers, not the first line).
5. Every `gh workflow run oracle-review-shadow.yml` command in docs and the Makefile names the new file.

Guardrails.
- The new status context must not equal any required check name in the develop ruleset (it must not be `oracle-review`); a commit status with a required name could satisfy the required context without the checker running. Check the ruleset's required contexts before choosing.
- Never weaken the required `oracle-review` check or the stand-in rule. The stand-in line `Stand-in oracle review: APPROVE <sha>` is unchanged.
- Very-high tier: the checker, workflow and reviewer package are gate paths. The PR's own oracle review runs develop's code under the old name, which is expected.
- Do not rename the required check (`oracle-review`, .github/workflows/oracle-review.yml) or the App.
- Worktree via `make worktree-create BRANCH=feat/<slug> ...` and `make agent-write-preflight`; identity Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>; explicit staging (use `git mv` for the workflow file); no comments or docstrings; `make comment-policy-check`.

Decision gates.
- Gate 1, before the first commit: confirm the new name with the owner. Proposed default: `oracle-verdict` (status context, first line, workflow file `oracle-verdict.yml`, artifacts `oracle-verdict-*`).
- Gate 2: if reading state under both the old and new workflow path makes `github.trusted_run` or the state lookup ambiguous, stop and ask whether to keep the workflow file and artifact prefix unchanged and rename only the posted text and status context.
